subject: Post-call recap: Acme integration — cost/TCO summary and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Acme integration — cost/TCO summary and next steps

Hi Jamie — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and the cost / TCO levers we discussed so your finance and engineering partners have something to review.

Pain points and goals we heard
- Current latency and token spend are driving >$25k/month on your hosted vendor; unpredictability when traffic spikes is a concern.
- Goal: reduce unit cost and get predictable monthly spend under ~$20k while keeping 90th p99 latency under 400ms for search and contextual generation flows.
- Needs: security controls (VPC + audit logs), predictable throughput for peak traffic, and a short pilot before procurement signs off.

High-level consumption and unit economics (quick baseline)
- Estimated monthly tokens (input + output): ~1.0B tokens.
- Hosted (no reservation) baseline: $0.00003 per token (~$30k/month).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) example: committed pool + autoscale = lower unit economics; effective starting point ~$0.000018 per token before batching/caching (~$18k/month on 1B tokens).

Cost levers we can apply to meet Acme goals
1) Batching and pipeline tuning — with continuous batching and request-shaping we typically reduce per-token compute by ~15-30% depending on QPS shape.
2) KV/prefix caching — for high-reuse prompts (search snippets, common contexts) we often see ~10-25% token reduction because we only generate deltas.
3) Quantized model variants / optimized kernels — 8-bit/4-bit variants and kernel selection can reduce GPU hours and enable lower reserved capacity.
4) Reservation + committed discount — modest monthly commit brings unit cost down significantly vs on-demand.

Workback (example adjusted estimate)
- Baseline hosted: $30k/mo (1B tokens at $0.00003/token).
- Apply batching (~20%) and KV caching (~15%) => ~35% effective reduction in billable compute => effective spend ~$19.5k/mo.
- With a 12-month committed Dedicated discount (we can model at mom), we can push to ~$15k-$18k/mo depending on commit and instance type.

Attachments
- ACME_TCO_v1.xlsx (attached) — workbook with line-item assumptions and alternate scenarios (hosted vs dedicated / POC sizing).

Proposed next steps
1) Share the workbook with your finance and infra leads (attached).
2) 30–45 minute follow-up with SRE to confirm QPS shape and cacheable prefix distributions.
3) Proposal: 1-month pilot on a small dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent) + integration support; if pilot matches throughput/latency expectations, convert to 12-month commit for unit cost improvements.

If this aligns with your priorities, I can: (a) rework the attached workbook to hit your $20k/mo target with concrete sizing and instance SKU recommendations, and (b) draft a one-page pilot SOW for procurement.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jamie Park <jamie.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme integration — cost/TCO summary and next steps

Marissa — really appreciate the recap and the workbook. A few clarifying notes from finance/procurement side:

- Current internal target is ~ $20k/month all-in for production (pilot can be higher but finance will sign off only if we can see a path to the $20k target within 60 days).
- Procurement timeline: we need a commercial term sheet and POC SOW by the end of May to hit our Q2 procurement cycle.
- Technical ask: SRE wants an estimate of p99 latency at the expected peak QPS (we'll share exact traces after the follow-up).

Can you: 1) produce a variant of the workbook that prioritizes hitting sub-$20k/mo (even if it requires a 12-month commit), and 2) outline the pilot SOW with clear exit criteria (latency, throughput, and cost delta)?

Thanks — Jamie
Jamie Park
Product Manager, AI Platform | Acme Corp
jamie.park@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jamie Park <jamie.park@acme.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Acme integration — cost/TCO summary and next steps

Jamie — thanks for the quick note and the timeline. I re-ran the workbook with a $20k target and a 12-month commit option — attaching the updated tab in ACME_TCO_v1.xlsx and a draft one-page SOW (Redwood_PO_20270420.pdf stub). Highlights below: 

Revised estimate to meet $20k target (example scenario)\- Starting consumption: 1.0B tokens/mo
- Optimizations applied: batching (20% reduction), KV/prefix caching (15% effective reduction), quantized model profile (additional ~10% on compute) => combined effective reduction ~40% (compound).
- Committed 12-month Dedicated pool (moderate commit level) drops per-token to ~$0.000015 => adjusted spend ~ $15k/mo in the modeled scenario.
- Conservative estimate (lower cache hit and less batching): ~$19k–$20k/mo.

Pilot SOW summary (one-page)
- Duration: 30 days pilot
- Scope: integration + routing + prefix cache configuration + 24/7 runbook for peak window
- Exit criteria: p99 latency < 400ms on benchmarked peak workload; successful integration of prefix cache with <10% missed-cache rate; observed cost <= 120% of modeled pilot spend.

Next steps I propose
1) SRE deep-dive: please share a 60-minute slot this week for us to validate QPS shape.
2) Procurement: I will draft a one-page pilot SOW and a commercial term sheet we can iterate on; expect draft by EOD tomorrow.
3) Internal: Rafael / Monica — can you review the attached pricing tab and confirm the 12-month commit tier that yields the ~15k/mo outcome so I can include SKU/commit language in the term sheet?

Attaching: Redwood_PO_20270420.pdf (pilot SOW stub) and updated ACME_TCO_v1.xlsx tab.

Best,
Marissa

--
Attachment: Redwood_PO_20270420.pdf (PDF, 45KB stub)

Subject: Internal: Acme pilot — pricing/discount approval request

Rafael / Monica — looping you both in for quick approval so we can hit Acme's procurement window. Key ask: provide a committed 12-month pricing tier that gets us to the $15k–$18k/mo modeled outcome (this is what finance at Acme needs to greenlight).

Summary / ask
- Modeled scenario in ACME_TCO_v1.xlsx: 1B tokens/month with combined optimizations (batching + KV caching + quantization) => ~40% effective reduction.
- Proposed commercial approach: 12-month commit with an initial 20% committed discount off list Dedicated unit price + standard enterprise support.
- If we can offer a 20% discount and include a 30-day pilot SOW, we believe Acme will sign for the 12-month commit.

Please advise if 20% is doable (or suggest an alternative %) and confirm which SKU/commit levels map to the modeled $15k/mo. Monica — can you draft a one-page SOW based on the attached pilot stub once Rafael confirms pricing?

I need a reply by EOD so I can send the term sheet to procurement tomorrow.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
